In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TDM is not routinely recommended, but that there are several scenarios where it may be indicated.

TDM in HIV-infected children is indicated when: 1. the patient has been treated with an antiretroviral (ARV) regimen for at least 3 months; 2. the patient has a suboptimal virological or immunological response to ARV therapy, or a suboptimal pharmacokinetic profile; and 3. the patient has an adverse reaction to an ARV drug.
TDM should not be considered a routine measurement as yet, although it may have added value in specific situations.

TDM may be helpful in the management of HIV infected children, especially in the following situations: (i) when the child has been on treatment for a prolonged time; (ii) when the child is experiencing virological failure; (iii) when the child experiences adverse events; (iv) when the child’s weight is less than 20 kg; (v) when the child presents with a viral load > 1000 copies/ml.
